Definition: from G4253 and G1728; to commence already:--begin (before).
BiblicalUsage: Proenarchomai means to commence already, to have begun before. Paul uses it twice for the Corinthians: Titus had begun the grace of giving among them, and they had begun before, not only to do, but also to be forward a year ago.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a good beginning deserves a good finishing, and the grace that started the giving must carry it through.
